text:
Maria: Quick heads-up — we're scheduling a slim runtime base-image rebuild next week to remove a few C libs and trim attack surface. Need to confirm KMS key access paths and RBAC for the image-bake service account.
Jamal: +1. which key? is this the cosign key in projects/prod-keystore?
Maria: yes, cosign signing key alias: projects/redwood/keystore/cosign-prod. We need a short-lived binding so infra-bake can sign during CI.
Oliver: Are we planning to use an operator or ephemeral keywrap for the baker? prefer not to give long-lived write to the keystore.
Kevin: We can do a kms:Sign delegate with a condition on principal and timeframe. Example IAM binding I tested:
```
resource: serviceAccount: infra-baker@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
role: roles/cloudkms.signer
condition: request.time < Timestamp("2026-04-01T00:00:00Z")
```
Kevin: That plus a narrow key ring name should be fine.
Maria: Good. Two follow-ups: 1) audit logging — ensure KMS Sign calls go to secure logging and are routed to the security project. 2) RBAC changes need CS approval before merge.
sec-bot: Note: upcoming change will touch image-bake pipeline. Runbook checklist: generate SBOM, cosign sign, push attestation, run vuln-scan. See https://internal.redwood.dev/runbooks/image-rebuild for steps.
oncall: Oncall FYI — schedule a light canary immediately after bake (staging only), and enable verbose runtime audit for 24h.
Jamal: For audit: we should add a log-based metric on KMS Sign failures + unusual signer principal usage. I can add rules to SIEM.
Maria: Jamal please own SIEM rule. Oliver, can you draft the RBAC PR with the conditional binding and the least-priv SA policy? Put it in infra repo and tag @security-review.
Oliver: Will do. Draft ETA EOD today. Also adding a temporary workload identity mapping for baker to avoid long-lived keys.
Kevin: One more operational detail: cosign key rotation — after the bake we should rotate the signing key and re-sign images if anything changed. That prevents token reuse.
Maria: Good catch. Add rotation window to the PR. Also add steps for incident rollback: if a signed image is found vulnerable, here's the quick rollback: 1) revoke signer key alias 2) mark image as deprecated in registry 3) route traffic to previous canary tag.
sec-bot: Security checklist item added: record artifact provenance in attestations and store SBOM in GCS bucket gs://redwood-sbom/image-rebuild-2026-03.
Jamal: For vuln triage, I propose triage cadence: T+0 (immediate triage by oncall + sec), T+4h (patch decision), T+24h (rollout or rollback). Agree?
oncall: Agreed. I'll be primary T+0 and handle alerts.
Maria: Awesome. Oliver, tag me in the PR. Jamal, leave SIEM rule details in the ticket. I'll coordinate the bake window Wed 01:00-03:00 UTC to minimize traffic.
Oliver: PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/infra-bake/pulls/412 — includes conditional binding, WID mapping, and bake job changes.
Jamal: SIEM rule created, tests pending.
Maria: Thanks everyone. After canary passes, we'll schedule Dedicated fleet cutover. :thumbsup:
Kevin: I'll schedule the rotation and update the keyowner doc.
Maria: Closing the thread — will ping again when canary completes.
